title: Toeplitz Matrix
spaceBreakdown:
- loop variables i, j, m, n: constant space → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no auxiliary arrays
- not counted: input matrix
approach: A matrix is Toeplitz if every element equals its top-left neighbor (the element one row up and one column left). We iterate over all cells (i, j) with i ≥ 1 and j ≥ 1, and check whether matrix[i][j] == matrix[i-1][j-1]. If any pair differs, the diagonal is broken and we return false; otherwise the matrix is Toeplitz. This works because two cells on the same top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal differ by exactly (+1, +1) in coordinates, so checking adjacent diagonal neighbors transitively verifies the entire diagonal.
hints: For an element at position (i, j) where both i and j are greater than 0, which other single element in the matrix must share the same value for its diagonal to be consistent?
Compare each element with its top-left neighbor matrix[i-1][j-1]. In Example 1, matrix[1][1] = 1 matches matrix[0][0] = 1, confirming that diagonal is consistent.

**Single cell** - 1×1 matrix has no neighbor pairs to check.
`Input: [[5]]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: starting the outer loop at i = 0 and accessing matrix[i-1][j-1] → out-of-bounds access / crash

**Single row** - every element is its own diagonal of length 1.
`Input: [[1,2,3]]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: not skipping i = 0 and reading matrix[-1][j-1] → out-of-bounds access / crash

**All equal** - every diagonal is trivially consistent.
`Input: [[7,7],[7,7]]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: inverting the comparison to `if (matrix[i][j] == matrix[i-1][j-1]) return false` → returns false

**Diagonal mismatch** - two cells on the same diagonal differ.
`Input: [[1,2],[2,2]]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: comparing with matrix[i-1][j] (directly above) instead of matrix[i-1][j-1] (top-left) → matrix[1][1]=2 equals matrix[0][1]=2, passes, returns true

followUps.q: What if the matrix is stored on disk and you can only load one row into memory at a time?
followUps.a: Load rows sequentially and keep only the previous row in a buffer of size n. For each new row, compare element at column j (j ≥ 1) with the previous row's element at column j-1. TC: O(m × n), SC: O(n) for one row buffer.

followUps.q: What if you can only load a partial row (k columns) into memory at a time?
followUps.a: Process the matrix in vertical strips of width k. Keep the last element of the previous row's strip to compare with the first element of the current row's adjacent strip. TC: O(m × n), SC: O(k).

followUps.q: What if you need to check whether a specific submatrix [r1..r2][c1..c2] is Toeplitz?
followUps.a: Apply the same neighbor comparison but only within the submatrix bounds: for each cell (i, j) with r1 < i ≤ r2 and c1 < j ≤ c2, check matrix[i][j] == matrix[i-1][j-1]. TC: O((r2-r1) × (c2-c1)), SC: O(1).
